confidence_notes: I ran two web searches. Beer, coffee, the inexpensive meal and the mid-range meal for two are based on GBP figures summarised in the search results. Those figures came from Expatica, which uses Numbeo data from about June 2026, plus MyLifeElsewhere and Expat Arrivals (October 2025). They were roughly £5.3 for a pint, £3.46 for a cappuccino, £15 for an inexpensive meal and about £65.8 for a three-course meal for two. I converted these to USD at an assumed GBP/USD rate of about 1.33. That rate was not looked up, so it adds some uncertainty to every anchor. Cocktail and wine prices were not checked directly. I estimated them from local price ratios to beer (a cocktail at about £10, a glass of wine at about £6.50), so they are less certain. The accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates for July, which is Cardiff's peak season. I did not check any booking sites. Prices can rise sharply on major event and concert dates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cardiff is treated as a mid-sized British regional capital. Its prices are similar to Bristol and Newcastle and somewhat below London, at roughly 10-28% less for restaurants and beer according to the comparison summaries.
